key_insight: Slow viscous flow in a triangular cavity generates a self-similar cascade of corner vortices whose sizes, strengths, and fractal dimensions follow Moffatt-style scaling.
engineering_relevance: Understanding this vortex fractal scaling helps predict corner-flow behavior in low-Reynolds-number devices and geometries where recirculation affects mixing, drag, and heat transfer.
method: Solved incompressible Navier–Stokes equations with a pressure-based coupled numerical solver.
Extracted successive corner vortices and measured their size and intensity ratios.
Applied the area–perimeter method to estimate fractal dimension and tested scaling across Reynolds numbers and cavity shapes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic numerical analysis showing non-integer fractal dimensions between 1 and 2, with consistent size/intensity scaling and a comparative self-similarity check for triangular versus square cavities.
watch_item: The empirical fractal-dimension relation may depend on grid resolution and vortex detection accuracy, so results should be validated carefully for different meshes and corner geometries.
paper_title: Fractal Scaling of Moffatt Vortices in Triangular Cavity Flow
